answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with unique location proofs. Each identity must prove it operates from a distinct geographic location, verified by independent attestations, and the network rejects identities that share a location. A farm in one data center cannot mint many identities, because they would all report the same place. Like jade set in copper, each identity is fixed in its own setting, and like a willow, it grows where it stands. Each extra fake needs its own distinct location with its own network presence, a cost that cannot be shared, parallelized, or bought in bulk.
